references.text: God promises to restore his people and cleanse the land, which aligns with the promise of reconciliation for the land and the people.
The nations shall praise Israel's God, reflecting the call for Gentiles to rejoice with his people.
The psalmist asks that vengeance for the blood of servants be made known among the nations, directly mirroring the theme of God's vengeance for the blood of his servants.
God is called the God of vengeance who will repay the proud, which corresponds to the promise of taking vengeance on enemies.
The day of the Lord's vengeance and the year of recompense for Zion's cause, reflecting God's judgment upon enemies.
The day of vengeance is in God's heart, and the year of redemption has come, reflecting the themes of vengeance and deliverance.
The martyrs cry out that God should avenge their blood on the inhabitants of the earth, a direct parallel to vengeance for the blood of servants.
God has judged the great prostitute and avenged the blood of his servants, fulfilling the promise of vengeance for the blood of servants.
Paul directly quotes this verse and applies it to the inclusion of Gentiles in God's people.
The book of Hebrews quotes from the same context and confirms that vengeance belongs to the Lord and he will repay.
